title: Spaghetti alla Carbonara
subtitle: Roman pasta with guanciale, egg, and Pecorino
excerpt: The Roman original: spaghetti tossed with crispy guanciale, an emulsion of egg yolks and Pecorino Romano, and freshly cracked black pepper. No cream, no onion, no garlic. The emulsification technique is everything.

recipe.sourceNotes: Carbonara is a Roman pasta dish whose origins are debated but most likely date to the post-World War II period, when American soldiers brought eggs and bacon to central Italy, and local cooks combined them with pasta. The defining technique is the emulsification of egg yolks (and sometimes one whole egg) with Pecorino Romano (or Parmigiano-Reggiano) to create a glossy, thick sauce that coats the pasta without curdling. The heat of the just-drained pasta, combined with some pasta cooking water, sets the sauce to a creamy consistency; too much heat curdles it into scrambled eggs. Guanciale (cured pig cheek) is the traditional cut; pancetta is the closest substitute. The dish has no cream — this is a common error, and the correct consistency is achieved entirely through the egg emulsion.

content.text: The critical moment is adding the egg mixture to the pasta: the pan must be off the heat and the pasta must be moving continuously. Too hot and the eggs scramble; too cold and the sauce does not set. A little pasta water loosens the emulsion and helps it coat evenly. Pecorino Romano is sharper and saltier than Parmesan; use it if you can find it.

items.preparation: guanciale preferred; cut into small lardons
Pecorino Romano preferred; finely grated; plus more to serve

content.text: Whisk the egg yolks, whole egg, and cheese together. Season with black pepper. Set aside. Cook the guanciale in a large dry frying pan over medium heat until the fat has rendered and the pieces are crispy. Remove from the heat.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 200 ml of the pasta cooking water. Drain the pasta and immediately add it to the frying pan with the guanciale (off the heat).

Add 50 ml of the pasta water to the egg mixture to loosen it. Pour the egg mixture over the pasta and toss vigorously for 1 to 2 minutes until the sauce is glossy and coats the pasta. Add more pasta water a little at a time if the sauce is too thick. Serve immediately with extra cheese and black pepper.
